'''Christopher Scott Hill''' is an American [[particle physicist]] and Professor of Physics at [[The Ohio State University]]. He is known for his contributions to the study of the [[top quark]] and for co-founding the [[milliQan Experiment]] at the [[Large Hadron Collider]].

== Early life and education ==
Hill was born in [[Bayport, New York]]. He graduated from Bayport-Blue Point High School in 1990. He earned his A.B. in physics and philosophy from [[Dartmouth College]] in 1994. He then attended the [[University of California, Davis]], where he received his M.S. and Ph.D. in physics in 1998 and 2001, respectively, under the supervision of Richard Lander.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Hill |first=Christopher Scott |title=Measurement of the production cross-section ratio top anti-top + jets to top anti-top inclusive in 106.0 +/- 4.1 pb(-1) of data collected by CDF during Run 1A + 1 $B$ of the Tevatron |year=2001 |doi=10.2172/1421393 |osti=1421393}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 1998 to 2001, Hill conducted doctoral research on the [[CDF experiment]] at [[Fermilab]], studying top quark properties in proton-antiproton collisions. He continued this research as a postdoctoral fellow at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] from 2001 to 2006, where he was responsible for commissioning and operating the CDF silicon tracking detector—the largest of its kind at the time. During this period, Hill and his supervisor [[Joe Incandela]] developed the "decay-length method" for measuring the top quark mass, utilizing the Lorentz boost of bottom quarks in top decay.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hill |first1=C. S. |last2=Incandela |first2=J. |title=A method for measurement of the top quark mass using the mean decay length of $b$ hadrons in $t\bar{t}$ events |journal=Physical Review D |date=2005 |volume=71 |issue=5 |article-number=054029 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.71.054029|arxiv=hep-ex/0501043 }}</ref>

In 2006, Hill became a lecturer in physics at the [[University of Bristol]], shifting his research to physics beyond the [[Standard Model]] with the [[CMS experiment]] at the LHC at [[CERN]]. He was an early proponent of searching for "[[long-lived particle]]s" (LLPs) at the LHC,<ref>{{cite web |last=Hill |first=C. |title=Disappearing tracks and other "tricky" experimental signatures |url=https://pirsa.org/15040081 |website=Perimeter Institute Recorded Seminar Archive |date=April 2015 |access-date=October 16, 2023}}</ref> which has since become a significant area of research in high-energy physics.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Knapen |first1=Simon |last2=Lowette |first2=Steven |title=A Guide to Hunting Long-Lived Particles at the LHC |journal=Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science |volume=73 |pages=421–449 |year=2023 |doi=10.1146/annurev-nucl-101920-013011|arxiv=2212.03883 |bibcode=2023ARNPS..73..421K }}</ref>

In 2010, Hill joined [[The Ohio State University]] as an associate professor, becoming a full professor in 2014. From 2012 to 2014, he served as deputy physics coordinator of the CMS experiment during the discovery of the [[Higgs boson]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Chris Hill appointed Deputy Physics Coordinator of the CMS Physics Program |url=https://physics.osu.edu/news/professor-chris-hill-appointed-deputy-physics-coordinator-cms-physics-program |website=The Ohio State University Department of Physics |access-date=October 16, 2023}}</ref>

In 2014, Hill co-founded the [[milliQan Experiment]] to search for millicharged particles, potential candidates for dark matter.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ball |first1=A. |last2=Beacham |first2=J. |last3=Boyd |first3=J. |last4=Buckley |first4=A. |last5=Cerri |first5=O. |last6=Curtin |first6=D. |last7=Essig |first7=R. |last8=Feng |first8=J. L. |last9=Gershtein |first9=Y. |last10=Gori |first10=S. |last11=Haas |first11=A. |last12=Hill |first12=C. S. |title=A Letter of Intent to Install a Milli-Charged Particle Detector at LHC P5 |journal=Physics Letters B |date=2016 |volume=751 |pages=376–379 |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2015.04.062|arxiv=1410.6816 }}</ref> He has served as co-spokesperson of the milliQan collaboration since its inception.

== Awards and honors ==
* Fermilab LPC Distinguished Researcher (2016)<ref>{{cite web |title=2016 LPC Distinguished Researchers |url=https://lpc.fnal.gov/fellows/index_2016.shtml |website=Fermilab |access-date=October 16, 2023}}</ref>
* Elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (2016) "For contributions to silicon tracking detectors at hadron colliders and for the development of novel analysis techniques, particularly those used in the searches for beyond the standard model particles with long lifetimes."<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2016&unit_id=DPF&institution=Ohio+State+University |website=American Physical Society |access-date=October 16, 2023}}</ref>
